name: io.github.2016judea/appeal-the-denial
title: Appeal the Denial
description: Paste your health insurance denial, get the appeal and the deadlines

tools.name: read_denial_letter
tools.description: Use when someone pastes or uploads a health insurance denial, EOB or adverse benefit determination. Pass the letter text verbatim. Returns what was denied, the reason category, the plan type (employer/ERISA, Marketplace, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid), the appeal deadline computed from the regulation, the next step and a draft appeal letter. The optional fields correct something the person stated. Deadlines are computed in code from the cited regulation. The tool does not assess medical necessity.

letter_text.description: The full text of the denial letter, verbatim

plan_type.description: Set only if the letter or the person says so: erisa = Employer plan (private employer, covered by ERISA); gov_employer = Government employer plan (state, county, city or school district); aca_individual = Individual or Marketplace (ACA) plan; medicare_advantage = Medicare Advantage plan; medicaid_managed = Medicaid managed care plan; medicaid_ffs = Medicaid (state agency, no managed care plan); original_medicare = Original Medicare; fehb = Federal employee plan (FEHB)

letter_date.description: Date printed on the letter, if the reader missed it

received_date.description: Day the person actually received the letter, if they say

stage.description: pre_service = prior authorization, post_service = a claim for care already given, concurrent = ongoing care being cut

urgent.description: True only if the person or their doctor says waiting could seriously harm their health. Never infer it.

internal_appeal_level.description: final = this letter denies an appeal already filed

self_funded.description: Employer plan paid by the employer itself (often 'self-funded', 'claims administrator')

two_level_appeals.description: Employer plan with two internal appeal levels

tools.name: appeal_deadlines
tools.description: Compute health insurance appeal deadlines when there is no letter text, only facts: plan type and the date on the denial. Returns each deadline with the regulation it comes from, computed in code. The tool does not assess medical necessity.

tools.name: how_long_to_appeal_insurance_denial
tools.description: How long a person has to appeal a health insurance denial, for each plan type or one: employer (ERISA), government employer, Marketplace, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, Original Medicare, FEHB. With a plan type and the letter date it returns the exact date; without them it returns the window for every plan type, counted for a letter dated today, each with its regulation. Example questions: how long do I have to appeal an insurance denial; what is the deadline to appeal a Medicare Advantage denial; is it too late to appeal.

tools.name: appeal_denied_again_what_next
tools.description: What comes after a health insurance appeal is denied: the next level for the plan type (independent external review, the automatic independent review for Medicare Advantage, a state fair hearing for Medicaid, court), the deadline for it computed from the date of the final denial, and a draft request. Example questions: my insurance appeal was denied, what now; the final denial came, can I still fight it; second appeal denied.

tools.name: independent_external_review
tools.description: Independent external review of a health insurance denial: what it is (a reviewer outside the insurer decides, and the plan pays if they side with the person), who can ask (not grandfathered plans), the four-month deadline computed from the final denial, the expedited version, and the regulation text verbatim. Example questions: what is an external review; how do I get an independent review of my denial; deadline for external review.

tools.name: urgent_insurance_appeal
tools.description: Expedited appeals for when the person or their doctor says waiting could seriously harm their health: how fast the plan has to decide (72 hours for employer, Marketplace, Medicare Advantage and Medicaid plans), the filing deadline, the expedited external review that can run at the same time, and the rule text verbatim. Example questions: I need surgery next week and it was denied; can I get a faster insurance appeal; how long does an urgent appeal take.

Example questions: my prior authorization was denied; insurance won't pre-approve my MRI; how to appeal a prior auth denial.

tools.name: medical_necessity_denial
tools.description: A denial that says the care was not medically necessary: the appeal path and deadline for the plan type, the rule that the appeal considers new evidence (such as a letter from the person's doctor), the right to the claim file, and a draft appeal built for this reason. It does not judge whether the care was necessary. Example questions: insurance says it's not medically necessary; how to fight a medical necessity denial; what to put in an appeal for a necessity denial.

tools.name: get_my_claim_file
tools.description: The right to a free copy of the claim file (every document, record and guideline the insurer relied on) for employer, government employer and Marketplace plans, with the regulation text verbatim and a short request letter with blanks to fill. For other plan types it says no rule for this is held here. Example questions: how do I get the records my insurer used to deny me; can I see my claim file; request the documents behind my denial.

Example questions: write my insurance appeal letter; appeal letter template for a denied claim; help me write a Medicare reconsideration request.
